title: arxiv_2602.22941v2
universal_lens: A mathematical lens unifying velocity and stroke rate reconstruction via homography estimation and optical flow tracking in panned zoomed video. A unified framework for multi-athlete canoe/kayak trajectory reconstruction using 4K video, GPS, and gyro data with automated tip offset calibration.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps video-derived kinematics to GPS-ground truth using probabilistic velocity and stroke rate models with uncertainty quantification. Bayesian inference models for probabilistic boat tip localization and stroke rate estimation using U-Net heatmaps and sensor fusion.
gse_mapping: Situationally-aware state transitions model athlete positioning and stroke dynamics through video frame sequences with adaptive tracking logic. Situational reasoning engine maps athlete positions to boat tip offsets, enabling real-time kinematic state transitions during races.

primitives.name: Velocity Profile Reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Pacing strategies, defined by velocity and stroke rate profiles, are essential for peak performance in canoe sprint.
primitives.assumptions: Velocity is reconstructed from calibrated video frames assuming constant boat length and known buoy grid.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When video perspective distortion exceeds 30 degrees or buoy grid is ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Maps 2D video coordinates to 3D velocity space via homography transformation.

primitives.name: Stroke Rate Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, we introduce methods to extract stroke rate information from either pose estimations or the athlete bounding boxes themselves.
primitives.assumptions: Stroke rate derived from periodic motion signals in athlete trajectory or bounding box centroid movement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When athlete occlusion or motion ambiguity exceeds 20% of frame sequence.

layer2.mapping: Derives stroke rate from temporal frequency of athlete displacement peaks.

primitives.name: Homography Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our method utilizes YOLOv8 for buoy and athlete detection, leveraging the known buoy grid to estimate homographies.
primitives.assumptions: Scene geometry is planar and buoy grid is accurately known; affine projection holds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When scene depth variation exceeds 10cm or buoy grid is misaligned.

layer2.mapping: Maps 2D image points to 3D world coordinates via projective transformation.

primitives.name: Optical Flow Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Further, we implement a robust tracking scheme using optical flow to adapt to multi-athlete boat types.
primitives.assumptions: Motion is locally constant and optical flow is dense across athlete bounding boxes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion blur exceeds 5 pixels or detection failure occurs in >10% frames.

layer2.mapping: Maintains athlete identity and position continuity via dense motion field estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Robustness to multi-athlete tracking under 20% detection loss
